page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions, but lacks AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-highcpu-8 delivers modest processing capabilities. Its Geekbench single-core score of 914.0 and multi-core score of 3557.0 place it in the poor and weak performance tiers respectively. Similarly, the stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks fall within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed; while cached small-block read operations are weak at 325.55 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write operations achieve average tier speeds of 47.28 GB/sec and 34.7 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates average performance in Geekbench ray tracing and LLM text generation for small 135M models, but shows poor results in single-threaded compression and text processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-8 offers a low-cost entry point for multi-core x86 workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained memory capacity of 7.0 GB for 8 vCPUs, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. Given the weak database operation benchmarks and low static web serving throughput of 5.09 GB/sec, this instance is best suited for lightweight parallel processing tasks, basic software compilation, and compute tasks with small memory footprints that can utilize multiple threads without exhausting the limited RAM.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 server instance in the n1 family, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical Intel Xeon cores) and 7.0 GB of memory. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it provides a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 0.9 GB per core. Benchmark results place its overall CPU performance in the weak to poor categories, with a Geekbench single-core score of 914.0 and multi-core score of 3557.0. However, it achieves average tier performance in uncached large-block memory bandwidth and Geekbench ray tracing. Qualitatively, the n1-highcpu-8 represents a budget-friendly option for compute-focused workloads with low memory demands. It is best suited for lightweight parallel processing, basic software compilation, and multi-threaded tasks that do not require substantial memory or high-speed local storage.
